whyItMatters: shell=True passes the command through a system shell, where metacharacters in attacker-influenced input become OS command injection.
actions: Drop shell=True and pass the command as an argument list so no shell is involved.
Never interpolate or concatenate input into a shell command; quote every dynamic fragment if a shell is unavoidable.
Add a regression test that passes metacharacters (spaces, quotes, semicolons) as input.
verification: No shell=True remains in the changed files and the metacharacter test passes.

example.caveat: shlex.split follows shell quoting rules; prefer an explicit argv list when the command is constructed in code.
